name: Grade 9 IIT: Data Products and Analysis
description: Charts, patterns, outliers, correlation, observations, inferences, conclusions, limitations, recommendations, dashboards, reports, Tinkercad mock-ups, and evidence-based presentations.

words.example: The chart showed the strongest pattern.

words.definition: A chart that uses bars to compare categories.
words.example: The bar chart compared survey choices.

words.definition: A chart that shows change over order or time.
words.example: The line chart showed a trend.

words.definition: A chart that uses points to compare two numerical variables.
words.example: The scatter plot suggested a correlation.

words.definition: A noticeable relationship or trend in data.
words.example: The pattern showed more responses in one category.

words.definition: A value very different from the rest.
A relationship where two things appear to change together.
words.example: The data suggested a possible correlation.
The tallest bar was an observation.

words.definition: An idea made from observations and evidence.
words.example: The inference explained why one category was high.

words.definition: A final statement about what the data shows.
A weakness or boundary that affects results.
words.example: Small sample size was a limitation.

words.definition: A suggested action based on evidence.
A visual summary of important data and findings.
words.example: The dashboard showed a chart and key conclusion.

words.definition: A visual product that explains information with text and graphics.
words.example: The infographic made the data easier to understand.

words.definition: A document or product that presents a question, evidence, and conclusion.
words.example: The one-page report included a limitation.

words.definition: A 3D design tool used to build digital models.
words.example: A Tinkercad model supported the data story.

words.definition: A simple model showing how a product could look.
words.example: The mock-up showed the data display idea.
Evidence statements used values from the chart.
